properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-CBC/PKCS7 with an Android Keystore key: FingerprintStorage encrypts the wallet password behind fingerprint unlock (transformation assembled at :86-88 from KeyProperties constants; Keystore keygen pinned to BLOCK_MODE_CBC at :164). Unauthenticated CBC — malleable without a separate MAC; fresh provider-generated IV per encryption, only the latest IV retained. Keystore keys are hardware-backed (key material not changeable, algorithm choice is); the file's own TODO notes it may be merged into Mo

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The 100,000-iteration constant feeding both KeyProviders' PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 — below OWASP's 600,000 for HMAC-SHA256. On the PIN path this is the weakest link: a 4-6 digit PIN's entropy is tiny and the KDF is the only brake on offline brute force from a stolen ciphertext. Same asset as ALG-4de3b020 (low-iterations view of it).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Static base64 IV literal ("testivdata123") in an androidTest — deliberately deterministic fixture for the SecurityGuard encryption tests; protects only test data. Kept as a true match so downstream can rank it by location (test sources); a production IV literal would be a real weakness.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Committed OpenSSH RSA public key in .deploy/ — deployment/CI automation key. Public half only (private counterpart lives in CI secrets), so no confidentiality exposure; but it pins deployment SSH authentication to RSA, quantum-vulnerable under Shor. Changeable here: swap the CI deploy key for ed25519 now, a PQ SSH key when supported.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: TopperClient (Uphold off-ramp integration) signs its authentication JWT with ES256 — ECDSA over P-256 with SHA-256, through jjwt 0.11.5 with Spongy Castle as the JCA provider. Quantum-vulnerable signature, deadline-class: a CRQC forges client tokens. Changeable here (integration module), but JWT has no PQ signature suite in wide deployment yet — migration is a protocol decision with the Topper API (EdDSA as an interim candidate, ML-DSA when JWS support lands).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-GCM (AES/GCM/NoPadding) is the authenticated workhorse of the wallet's at-rest stack: ModernEncryptionProvider (Keystore-backed, keygen pinned to BLOCK_MODE_GCM at :184), DualFallbackEncryptionProvider (:64, :331-332 — dual-provider fallback), ModernEncryptionMigration (:58, :220-221 — legacy-GCM path), and DashConnect's KeyExchangeCrypto (:178-220 — AES-256-GCM session encryption after secp256k1 ECDH+HKDF). properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Canonical entry for the PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 derivation: JCA SecretKeyFactory + PBEKeySpec stretch a user mnemonic (MnemonicBasedKeyProvider :44/:75-76 — 256-bit AES key for "Forgot PIN" recovery, salt = "dash_wallet_<alias>", deterministic) or numeric PIN (PinBasedKeyProvider :44/:65-66) into the SecurityGuard's keys. 100,000 iterations — weakness view is ALG-a861135a; the HMAC-SHA-256 object (ALG-ce74cadc) is the PRF of this same call.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA256 appears here only as the PRF inside PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 — same SecretKeyFactory calls as ALG-4de3b020, not a standalone MAC over application data. PQ-comfortable; no migration needed; kept so the CBOM records the PRF.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jjwt-api 0.11.5 — the JWT API surface the Uphold integration compiles against; TopperClient's ES256 signing (ALG-36874020) is its one consumer found. JCA-based; supports HS*/RS*/ES*/PS* and the build ships them whether or not all are used. This IS the dependency inventory for the integration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jjwt-impl 0.11.5 — runtime implementation of the jjwt API, declared alongside jjwt-api; the ES256 signing in TopperClient executes through it.
